scenes.title: Managed Data Warehouses
scenes.narration: Cloud data warehouses like Redshift, BigQuery, and Synapse are built to run fast analytical queries over huge datasets using columnar storage and massive parallelism.

scenes.title: Why They Are Fast
bullets: Columnar storage reads only the columns a query needs, slashing input and output.
Massively parallel processing splits a query across many nodes at once.
Compression and pruning reduce how much data is scanned per query.
scenes.narration: Warehouses store data by column rather than by row, so an analytical query touches only the columns it references. They then spread that work across many nodes in parallel, turning huge scans into fast results. Compression and partition pruning further cut the volume of data actually read.

scenes.title: OLTP vs. OLAP
scenes.narration: Transactional databases store rows and excel at many small reads and writes for applications. Analytical warehouses store columns and are tuned for scanning and aggregating vast amounts of data. Using each for its intended purpose is fundamental to a healthy data platform.

scenes.title: Architecture Styles
scenes.narration: Warehouses differ in how you manage capacity. Redshift traditionally provisions a cluster of nodes you size, while BigQuery is serverless and scales behind the scenes. Modern designs separate compute from storage so each can grow independently, a pattern now common across all three.

scenes.title: A Warehouse Analytical Query
scenes.narration: This example captures both the query and a crucial cost lesson. The aggregation groups sales by category, which is exactly the kind of scan-and-summarize work warehouses handle well. Because engines like BigQuery bill by the bytes scanned, selecting only needed columns and filtering on partitioned fields keeps both latency and cost down.

scenes.text: Cloud warehouses use columnar storage and parallelism to make big analytics fast — model for analytics, prune what you scan, and separate compute from storage.
scenes.narration: Cloud warehouses win on analytics through columnar layout and parallel execution. Model your data for aggregation, scan as little as possible, and lean on separated compute and storage to scale cost-effectively.
